title: buildtrace-manifest-orchestrator: generate reproducible release manifests and automated rollback bundles for private installer
author: Aditi Kapoor
description: Motivation: private deployments require deterministic, auditable release artifacts and easy rollback semantics for on-prem/VPC installs. Existing release artifacts were ad-hoc: signed tarballs and a single index.json. That made reconciling upgrades with operator Terraform state awkward and increased risk during emergency rollbacks. This PR introduces a manifest orchestrator that (1) emits reproducible, content-addressed release manifests (build-trace bundles) combining artifact checksums, build metadata, dependency pins, and optional SBOM links, (2) produces an automated rollback bundle that includes a Terraform state snapshot reference and Helm chart patch diffs, and (3) wires these bundles into the CI/CD pipeline so every private-installer release includes a machine-readable rollback manifest alongside the signed artifacts. What changed: new tooling in /ci/release-orchestrator that generates a build-trace file per release (build-trace-{sha}.jsonl.gz), a delta-rollback bundle under releases/{version}/rollback.tar.gz and a canonical content-addressable index (cas-index.json) used by the installer and upgrade tool. The orchestrator integrates with the existing signing step (sigstore/cosign) and the artifact registry: after artifacts are built, ci/release-orchestrator computes canonical tarball digests (strip timestamps, normalize owner/mode), collects build metadata (builder image, git commit, build environment), queries Helm to produce a diff patch from target to previous release, snapshots terraform plan output and stores a short-lived snapshot pointer in the release metadata. The CI pipeline changes (github/workflows/release-orchestrator.yml) run the orchestrator in a gated job after image build and before publishing to the release bucket. The installer (private-installer/installer) now consumes cas-index.json to resolve artifacts by digest and validates the build-trace signature at deploy time when running with --verify-release. Rollback UX: operators can download releases/{version}/rollback.tar.gz which contains: helm-chart-patch.diff, terraform-state-snapshot-pointer, and a pre-signed rollback manifest that the installer understands. Implementation notes: - A small Go binary (cmd/release-orchestrator) with deterministic tar creation (zero timestamps, stable file ordering) - A lightweight schema for build-trace entries (versioned; schema v1) designed for incremental extension - Helm diff generation uses helm template + kube-diff strategy to produce minimal diffs for safer application - Terraform integration stores a snapshot in a private S3-backed snapshot-store (pointer included, credentials readers required in enterprise envs) Testing and validation: - Unit tests for canonical tar creation and digest stability included - Integration test added to perf-canary that runs the orchestrator against a canned release and verifies index checksums and sign/verify roundtrip - E2E test simulates an upgrade and rollback using the generated rollback bundle (flaky network case identified and retried in CI) Backwards compatibility & migration: older installers ignore cas-index.json and continue to use index.json; new installers run additional verification when --verify-release is enabled. No breaking API changes to Helm charts; we add optional metadata fields. Rollout plan: ship to canary (internal staging) for 2 weeks, add migration TTL on CAS pointers, then flip default verify-release to on for Dedicated customers who opt in. Security and compliance: build-trace includes a minimal provenance blob; we do not embed secrets. Signing is performed via existing sigstore courier job and verified in CI with a separate key pair for private-installer releases. Caveats & Known issues: - Initial CI run failed helm-lint on chart metadata (fixed in subsequent commit) - Terraform snapshot TTL requires operator credential configuration in some air-gapped setups; documentation added in docs/private-installer/release-orchestrator.md Files and small diffs: changed files list below contains representative snippets and examples. Checklist: - [x] deterministic artifact generation - [x] signing + verification integration - [x] helm diff generation - [x] terraform snapshot pointer creation - [x] integration + e2e tests - [x] docs updated (private-installer release notes, operator guide) Related: builds on ENG-1023 and references SUP-78 for customer rollback requests. Links: jira:SUP-78, linear:ENG-1023.

release_notes: Add release-orchestrator: generates deterministic content-addressed manifests and automated rollback bundles for private-installer. Includes signing integration, helm diff export, and terraform snapshot pointers. Installers can opt-in to --verify-release for signature verification. See docs/private-installer/release-orchestrator.md for operator migration steps.
